{{Game Book |lorename=none |author=[[Skyrim:Hamelyn|Hamelyn]] |icon=SR-icon-book-Journal1.png |id=0010B2CD |value=75 |weight=1 |questrel=Dampened Spirits |loc=* Held by [[Skyrim:Hamelyn|Hamelyn]] }} <font face='$HandwrittenFont'> Ten years of ridicule. Ten years of imprisonment. Ten years of exile.
The children threw rocks and the women spat upon me as the menfolk dragged me into [[Skyrim:Whiterun|Whiterun]]'s prison. They branded me a danger to their pitiful existence... used words like "madman" and "insane." Could a madman escape the prisons undetected? Could a lunatic establish a laboratory right under their noses? Could a psychopath create a mighty army from the common [[Skyrim:Skeever|skeever]]?
My days as an apprentice alchemist in [[Skyrim:Winterhold|Winterhold]] were no better. Those egotistical braggarts couldn't compete with my abilities. Where they fell short, I'd constantly excel. Did they appreciate my genius? Did they relish my contributions? No. My instructors beat me and said I was irresponsible, and the {{sic|Arch Mage|Arch-Mage|description=missing hyphen}} cast me into the streets like a common beggar.
As my enemy grows complacent and weak, as they forget [[Skyrim:Hamelyn|Hamelyn]] and his utter brilliance, I build my army. I use every bit of knowledge at my disposal to forge their demise. Thanks to [[Skyrim:Sabjorn|Sabjorn]]'s unwitting assistance, my legion grows stronger every day. The irony that the same ingredients used to make his vile drink could be used to feed my offspring isn't lost upon me.
Oh, they will pay. Their ignorance of impending annihilation amuses me. I will bury Whiterun and watch Winterhold burn. And when they experience the fury I've unleashed upon them, when my progeny are gnawing the flesh from their bones, they will come begging and groveling at my feet. But there will be no mercy, no quarter and no leniency. And I will laugh and I will dance and I will rejoice over their mangled, broken corpses. The time for recompense has arrived.
Ten years of pain. Ten years of misery. Ten years of death. {{Book End}}

{{Artifact Summary |image=SR-item-Oghma Infinium.jpg |weight=1 |value=2500 |type=[[Skyrim:Books|Book]] |artifacttype=Daedric Artifact |editorid=DA04OghmaInfinium |objectid=0001A332 }} The [[Skyrim:Oghma Infinium|Oghma Infinium]] is a Daedric artifact acquired for completing the quest, [[Skyrim:Discerning the Transmundane|Discerning the Transmundane]]. Reading the book will give you the option to boost either your [[Skyrim:Combat|combat]], [[Skyrim:Magic Overview|magic]], or [[Skyrim:Stealth|stealth]] [[Skyrim:Skills|skills]] by five levels.
<includeonly>For more information, see the [[Skyrim:Oghma Infinium|Oghma Infinium]] article.</includeonly><noinclude>__NOTOC__{{NewLeft}} ---- {{Game Book |lorename=none |author=[[Lore:Xarxes (god)|Xarxes]] |description=An ancient text containing the knowledge of Hermaeus Mora |icon=SR-icon-book-OghmaInfinium.png |id=0001A332 |value=2500 |weight=1 |questrel=Discerning the Transmundane |loc=*[[Skyrim:Septimus Signus's Outpost|Septimus Signus's Outpost]] |coded=1 |nobox=1 |nodiv=1 }}{{#addtotrail:Artifacts|separator=' / '}}[[Category:Skyrim-Items-Artifacts]] [[File:SR-book-Oghma Infinium 1.png|center]] [[File:SR-book-Oghma Infinium 2.png|center]]
== Related Quests == *{{Quest Link|Discerning the Transmundane}}
==Notes== *You cannot use the Oghma Infinium to raise skills above 100. *The Oghma Infinium is removed from your inventory 1 second after choosing a skill and going back to the inventory. You can drop the book before it is removed and pick it up afterwards. However, this will not allow you to boost your skills again. *The text on the pages appears to be a variation of the [[Lore:Magic Script Alphabet|Magic Script Alphabet]]. This is most noticible on the three letters inside the sun symbols of the first page: the top right sun is inscribed with a "M" ([[File:MAGICSCRIPT_M.png|20px]]), the left sun is inscribed with a "S" ([[File:MAGICSCRIPT_S.png|15px]]), and the bottom sun is inscribed with a "G" ([[File:MAGICSCRIPT_G.png|25px]]).
==Bugs== {{Bug|When reading the Oghma Infinium from a bookshelf, the number of books that can be stored in that shelf increases by one each time the book is read.|OSP|1.9.26.0.8}} {{Bug|You may not always get all five points in each skill.}} ** Reload an older game and alter your skill values slightly, even just gaining a few more XP in the skill, then try again.
==See Also== For more information, see the [[Lore:Oghma Infinium|lore article]].</noinclude>

{{CC Header|Staff of Sheogorath}}[[Category:Skyrim-Staff of Sheogorath]][[Category:Skyrim-Creation Club-Books]]{{Game Book |lorename=none |author=[[Skyrim:Sheogorath|Sheogorath]] |description=A letter challenging the reader to an unorthodox combat trial |icon=SR-icon-book-TornNote.png |mod=[[Skyrim:Staff of Sheogorath|Staff of Sheogorath]] |id=FExxx80D |value=0 |weight=0 |quest=Put A Fork In It |loc=*Pinned to a keg inside [[Skyrim:The Retching Netch|The Retching Netch]] }} Dear person who happened upon this letter, it is your lucky day! Nearby you will find the [[Skyrim:Fork of Horripilation|Fork of Horripilation]]. Oh, how I do love cutlery! "But what is it?" you must be asking. Well, horripilation is the standing of hairs on end due to cold, fear, or excitement -- and excitement is indeed upon us, my friend! Take this fork, and use it to kill two special [[Skyrim:Bull Netch|Bull Netches]] in single combat. Each will yield an artifact: The [[Skyrim:Ciirta's Eye|Eye of Ciirta]], and the [[Skyrim:Branch of the Tree of Shades|Branch of the Tree of Shades]]. Warriors of another age might find these familiar. Combine these together with some [[Skyrim:Heart Stone|Heart Stones]] at a [[Skyrim:Staff Enchanter|Staff Enchanter]] for a special surprise! If you're successful, you'll be rewarded quite handsomely, with the [[Skyrim:Staff of Sheogorath (item)|Staff of Sheogorath]] (handsome, indeed!) If not, well... I do love to watch a good fight! Yours Truly,
Lord [[Skyrim:Sheogorath|Sheogorath]] {{Book End}}

{{CC Header|Headman's Cleaver}}[[Category:Skyrim-Headman's Cleaver]][[Category:Skyrim-Creation Club-Books]]{{Game Book |lorename=none |description=A brother plans to commit fratricide |icon=SR-icon-book-Journal2.png |mod=[[Skyrim:Headman's Cleaver|Headman's Cleaver]] |author=Urzog |id=FExxx811 |value=10 |weight=1 |loc=*Carried by [[Skyrim:Darkwater Snake|Darkwater Snake]] |quest=Blood in the Water |note=1 }} I've always beaten my little brother in everything. Cards, I had the better hands. Brawls, likewise. When we raced up the ramparts of the old castle, I would always be the first to reach the peak.
{{Lore Link|Urzoga gra-Batul|Mother}} said the difference between myself and my brother was that he was a perfectionist, and I was a conquerer. She said I wanted to beat him at everything, and it drove me to become a great warrior.
But my brother didn't care for competition. As a perfectionist, he simply wanted to sharpen his skills, and would work with others if he thought it would better himself.
Mother said that's why he would make the better {{Lore Link|Bloodfall|ruler}}. My brother would forever try to improve our standing, whereas I was content being better than the next man.
Well, little did she know the next man was him.
I'm going to enjoy killing you little brother. Grandfather's venom may have failed to reach mother's veins, but it will still reach her heart. {{Book End}}

{{CC Header|Civil War Champions}} [[Category:Skyrim-Civil War Champions]] [[Category:Skyrim-Creation Club-Books]]{{Game Book |lorename=none |author=[[SR:Legate Adventus Caesennius|Legate Adventus Caesennius]] |description= |icon=SR-icon-book-Note1.png |mod=[[Skyrim:Civil War Champions|Civil War Champions]] |id= |value=0 |weight=0 |quest= |loc= }} <Alias=Player>
A troop of [[SR:Stormcloaks|Stormcloak]] rebels have challenged us to a battle on the fields of [[SR:Whiterun Hold|Whiterun]]. They want us to send a garrison of our greatest champions to fight theirs. I've talked to [[SR:General Tullius|General Tullius]] and we can't rule out the possibility this is some kind of trap.
After all, the traitors have shown they have little concern for loyalty, it's doubtful they would give honor the same courtesy.
As one of our staunchest warriors, we'd like you to handle this mission. Our smiths have forged you a custom armor set that should offer some protection. We'll also send a garrison to support you, but we can't spare more than a half dozen men. Should things come to blows, you'll need to take the lead.
- [[SR:Legate Adventus Caesennius|Legate Adventus Caesennius]]
